ai.description: *Hemidactylus graniticolus* is a small gecko reaching 50 mm SVL. It is greyish-brown with dark dorsal blotches and a white venter. Distinctive features include a tuberculate dorsum and a tail with whorls.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hemidactylus graniticolus* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous series of enlarged, strongly keeled tubercles extending from the neck to the tail.
ai.habitat: *Hemidactylus graniticolus* inhabits rocky outcrops and granite boulders within dry deciduous forests and scrublands, typically at elevations between 300 and 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: *Hemidactylus graniticolus* is a nocturnal gecko that primarily hunts for insects on granite rock outcrops, where it uses its specialized toe pads to navigate vertical surfaces.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hemidactylus graniticolus* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of two hard-shelled eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, from June to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hemidactylus graniticolus* is endemic to the granite hillocks of the Eastern Ghats in the Indian states of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
